A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPLM-Evo research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably despite local revisions and relocated displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original computational results for ProteinGym variant prediction, protein generation, motif scaffolding, sequence-family expansion and GFP optimization, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original computational evaluations and their results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The latent-alignment framework, three prediction heads, binary indel losses and sampling algorithm are retained. The revised appendix reconciles its kernel description with the auxiliary masked-context formulation already in v1 Section 3.1 and specifies previously undocumented implementation details; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain UniRef50 training, ProteinGym substitution and indel evaluation, unconditional generation with SwissProt comparisons, motif scaffolding, CAMEO sequence-family expansion and GFP optimization. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparison methods in Figures 2–6 and Tables 1–3 remain the same, including the sequence, structure/MSA, generation and GFP baselines. Table 2 adds rows for DPLM-Evo itself, not new competing methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, 500 denoising steps, initial generation lengths, motif sampling and success criteria, and GFP search settings are retained. Appendix A.1.6 newly states that kernel comparisons share data and training hyperparameters; this documents the existing experiment rather than revising its protocol.

E4.justification: Kernel ablations, indel dynamics, diversity and repetition analyses, secondary-structure comparisons, assay-level breakdowns and editing case studies are retained. Appendix E's added introductory text and Figure 7's relocation introduce no new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and distribution plots. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported results remain unchanged, including indel Spearman 0.495 in Table 1, generation pLDDT 83.6 in Table 3, and GFP pTM 0.793/0.857 in Section 4.5. Table 2's added 0.420/0.459 entries repeat scores already stated in v1's caption; the plotted results are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the forward marginal's point mass to the clean sequence and fixes the loss sign and corruption indicator. Appendix A reconciles inconsistent kernel definitions and formalizes the confidence quantile. Section 4.1 removes the explicit GEMME-alignment KL objective. These are limited mathematical revisions, without a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the claim of negligible computational overhead. The central contributions and claims concerning evolutionary edits, single-sequence ProteinGym performance, variable-length generation and protein post-editing remain.

C2.justification: Appendices A.1.1 and A.1.4 replace assertions that noise lies on the protein manifold and represents high-fitness homologues with qualified descriptions of proximity to the natural-protein manifold and plausible homolog-like variants. Existing limitations concerning indels, approximate sampling and training overhead remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1.2–A.1.3 specify the single-sample kernel approximation and quantile rule for the previously unspecified dynamic threshold; A.1.6 clarifies matched ablation hyperparameters. V3 adds a planned code-release location but removes the explicit GEMME-alignment loss recipe. The PDFs do not establish an actual code release or changed training settings.

R1.justification: The same 59 references and Appendix C's positioning relative to EditFlow, DreamOn, diffusion models, protein language models and MSA-based methods are retained. Bibliographic styling changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 corrects wording and terminology, rewrites portions of Appendices A–B, and adds introductory paragraphs to Appendices D–E, acknowledgements and front-matter notes. The main section order and overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 2 adds rows displaying previously reported DPLM-Evo scores, Figure 2 explains its asterisk, and Figure 8's caption is corrected to describe its actual contents. Appendix figures, algorithms and tables are relocated, with local equation and reference formatting changes; plotted content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 improves internal consistency by correcting the preliminary equations, reconciling the appendix kernel with Section 3.1, specifying confidence-threshold selection and moderating biological interpretations. Removing the explicit GEMME-alignment loss reduces reproducibility detail, but the clarification and correctness gains support a limited net improvement. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
